summary: Reproduced the reserved-slot crash in follow_bootstrap_room_scheduler and changed bootstrap-room modulo routing to use the active-worker domain. Added regression coverage for reserved None sockets plus sparse and empty active-worker boundaries.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before run with the regression tests applied but the source unchanged: 3 failed, 3 passed. bootstrap_room=2 selected reserved workers[2]=None and raised AttributeError from sock_send; sparse and empty active-worker boundary tests also failed.

Passing-after focused controller suite: 20 passed, including reserved-slot routing to worker 0, sparse active-slot mapping, empty-active explicit failure, existing direct-rank behavior, and other scheduler budget tests.

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect is deterministic Python controller selection before any GPU/model execution. The regression uses mocked worker sockets and no GPU kernels; a gfx950 run would not add evidence for this routing calculation.
remaining_limitations: No live multi-worker disaggregated serving deployment was run; validation is the issue-specific controller regression and independent routing boundaries.
No model weights or semantic model output were exercised because the failure occurs before worker execution.

Upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34105 is open and has expanded into broader elastic-topology changes; this mirror patch intentionally addresses only the reported reserved-slot routing defect on the recorded base.
